test_title: PYST 79: SSC CGL 2024 - Quantitative Aptitude (Held On 26 Sept, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: maths
question: In a class of 150 students (boys and girls only), the girls are 60. The average weight of boys is 52 kg and that of girls is 48 kg. What is the average weight (in kg) of the whole class?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of Boys to Girls = (150 − 60) : 60 = 90 : 60 = 3 : 2.

Let the assumed average weight be 48 kg.

Deviation of boys' average from 48 kg = 52 − 48 = +4 kg.

Total deviation = 3 × 4 = +12 kg.

Net change in average = +12 ÷ (3 + 2) = +2.4 kg.

**∴ The correct answer is 50.4 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total students = 150

Number of girls = 60

Number of boys = 150 − 60 = 90

Average weight of boys = 52 kg

Average weight of girls = 48 kg

 
 Boys: 52
 
 Girls: 48
 
 Avg: x
 
 Ratio: 3
 
 Ratio: 2
 
• 
 
• 
 
• 
 
• 
 x − 48
 52 − x

**Formula Used:**

Using Alligation Rule, Ratio of Boys to Girls = (Avg of Girls − Combined Avg) : (Combined Avg − Avg of Boys)

**Calculation:**

⇒ Ratio of Boys to Girls = 90 : 60 = 3 : 2

Let the combined average weight of the class be x kg.

⇒ (x − 48) ÷ (52 − x) = 3 ÷ 2

⇒ 2 × (x − 48) = 3 × (52 − x)

⇒ 2x − 96 = 156 − 3x

⇒ 5x = 252

⇒ x = 50.4

**∴ The correct answer is 50.4 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average

When two groups of sizes N₁ and N₂ have averages A₁ and A₂, the combined average is given by (N₁ × A₁ + N₂ × A₂) ÷ (N₁ + N₂).

Alligation Rule

A quick method to find the ratio in which two groups are mixed. The ratio of quantity of group 1 to group 2 is (Mean − A₂) : (A₁ − Mean), assuming A₁ > Mean > A₂.

Deviation Method

Reduces calculation by assuming a base average. Net average = Assumed Average + (Total Deviation ÷ Total Items).
